title: Carbon and an introduction to organic chemistry
summary: Learn about carbon's bonds, its allotropes, the types of formulas and isomerism.
cards.0.p: Organic chemistry studies carbon compounds. Carbon is mostly bonded to H, and also to O, N and S. CO, CO₂, carbonates and cyanides, however, count as inorganic.
cards.0.svg#0: All contain C, but not all are organic
cards.0.etk.soru: All of these contain carbon. Which are organic compounds, and which are traditionally counted as inorganic?
cards.0.etk.ogeler.3.2: Urea, which Wöhler synthesized in 1828, is an organic compound.
cards.0.key: Carbides (such as CaC₂) are inorganic too. Pure carbon is not a compound at all.
cards.0.once.soru: All of these contain carbon. Which one is an organic compound?
cards.0.once.secenekler.0.neden: It is the simplest organic compound, with H bonded to C.
cards.0.once.secenekler.1.neden: CO₂ is traditionally counted as inorganic.
cards.1.h: Wöhler and the end of vital force
cards.1.p: People once believed that organic matter could only form in living things, through a vital force. In 1828, Wöhler made urea from inorganic ammonium cyanate.
cards.1.svg#8: Both have the molecular formula CH₄N₂O
cards.1.svg#9: No living thing, no vital force: organic matter formed
cards.1.key: This experiment shook the idea of vital force (vitalism). Later syntheses led to the idea being dropped completely.
cards.1.once.soru: Can an organic substance be made in the lab, without a living thing?
cards.1.once.secenekler.0.neden: Wöhler made urea from an inorganic substance. So a living thing is not required.
cards.1.once.secenekler.1.neden: That was the old vital force idea, and experiments disproved it.
cards.1.once.secenekler.2.neden: It can be synthesized in the lab without taking any substance from a living thing.
cards.2.p: Organic compounds are usually covalent. They have low melting points, most dissolve poorly in water, and they burn. Most inorganic compounds are ionic. They have high melting points, and their solutions conduct electricity.
cards.2.svg#21: General trends: there are exceptions (sugar dissolves well in water).
cards.2.key: These are only trends. Sugar, for example, is organic, but it dissolves very well in water.
cards.2.once.soru: You heat a candle and some table salt. Which one melts sooner?
cards.2.once.secenekler.0.neden: Wax is organic, and the attraction between its molecules is weak. So it melts at a low temperature.
cards.2.once.secenekler.1.neden: Salt is an ionic solid and melts at 801 °C.
cards.2.once.secenekler.2.neden: Their melting points are very different.
cards.3.p: Carbon has four valence electrons and forms four covalent bonds. With its own atoms, it builds long straight or branched chains and rings. It can form single, double and triple bonds.
cards.3.svg#23: Strong C–C bonds build long skeletons
cards.3.key: In stable organic compounds, C forms four bonds. C=C counts as two bonds and C≡C as three. Millions of organic compounds come from this property.
cards.4.p: Forms of the same element with different structures are called allotropes. In diamond, each C is bonded to four C atoms, and it is very hard. In graphite, each C is bonded to three C atoms, the layers slide, and it conducts electricity.
cards.4.key: Diamond does not conduct electricity. Allotropes are different forms of the same element. That is why both give CO₂ when they burn in enough O₂.
cards.4.once.soru: Why does a pencil tip (graphite) leave a mark on paper so easily?
cards.4.once.secenekler.0.neden: Graphite layers are held together by weak attraction. When rubbed on paper, the layers come apart and stay on the paper.
cards.4.once.secenekler.1.neden: Diamond is the hard one. Graphite is soft.
cards.4.once.secenekler.2.neden: Graphite does not melt while you write.
cards.5.p: Fullerene (C₆₀) is a molecule shaped like a soccer ball. Graphene is a single layer of graphite, one atom thick. A nanotube is graphene rolled into a cylinder, and it is both light and strong.
cards.5.key: C₆₀ has 12 pentagons and 20 hexagons. Graphene is very strong and an excellent conductor.
cards.5.once.soru: Which element are fullerene, graphene and nanotubes made of?
cards.5.once.secenekler.0.neden: They are all allotropes of carbon.
cards.5.once.secenekler.1.neden: Silicon is a different element. These structures contain only C.
cards.5.once.secenekler.2.neden: There is no metal in these structures.
cards.6.p: When carbon bonds, its orbitals mix and form hybrid orbitals. A C with four single bonds is sp³ (109.5°), a C with a double bond is sp² (120°), and a C with a triple bond is sp (180°) hybridized.
cards.6.key: CH₄ is tetrahedral, C₂H₄ is trigonal planar, and C₂H₂ is linear. A C with two double bonds is also sp hybridized.
cards.7.p: End-to-end overlap of orbitals forms a sigma (σ) bond, and side-by-side overlap forms a pi (π) bond. A single bond is 1σ, a double bond is 1σ + 1π, and a triple bond is 1σ + 2π.
cards.7.key: A σ bond is stronger than a π bond. The π bond prevents rotation. C–H bonds are σ bonds too.
cards.8.p: According to VSEPR theory, the electron pairs on the central atom repel each other and spread as far apart as possible. Lone pairs repel more strongly. That is why the angle is 109.5° in CH₄, 107° in NH₃ and 104.5° in H₂O.
cards.8.svg#24: A: central atom · X: bonded atom · E: lone pair
cards.8.key: In AXnEm notation, n is the number of bonded atoms and m is the number of lone pairs. A multiple bond counts as one direction. So CO₂ is AX₂ and linear.
cards.8.once.soru: Why is a water molecule bent rather than straight?
cards.8.once.secenekler.0.neden: The two lone pairs on O push the H atoms and narrow the angle to 104.5°.
cards.8.once.secenekler.1.neden: The two H atoms do not repel each other, but they do not attract either. Electron pairs decide the shape of the molecule.
cards.8.once.secenekler.2.yazi: The O atom is very small
cards.8.once.secenekler.2.neden: Electron pairs decide the shape, not atom size.
cards.9.p: A bond between atoms with different electronegativities is polar. If the bond dipoles do not cancel, the molecule is polar. H₂O and NH₃ are polar. Symmetric CH₄ and CO₂ are nonpolar.
cards.9.key: A polar bond does not mean a polar molecule. BF₃ is also nonpolar because it is symmetric.
cards.9.once.soru: The C=O bonds in CO₂ are polar. Is the molecule polar?
cards.9.once.secenekler.0.neden: In a linear molecule, the two dipoles point in opposite directions and cancel.
cards.9.once.secenekler.1.neden: Polar bonds are not enough. You also have to look at the molecule's geometry.
cards.9.once.secenekler.2.neden: Polarity depends on the molecule's shape, not its state.
cards.10.p: The molecular formula shows the number of atoms (C₄H₁₀), and the empirical formula shows the smallest ratio (C₂H₅). The structural formula shows every bond. In a skeletal formula, each corner is a C atom.
cards.10.key: A condensed formula shows the chain as groups. An empirical formula alone does not identify a molecule. For example, HCHO and glucose have the same empirical formula (CH₂O).
cards.11.h: Finding a formula by combustion analysis
cards.11.p: In combustion analysis, all the C ends up in CO₂ and all the H ends up in H₂O. From the products, you find the mass of C and H. If this total is less than the mass of the sample, the difference is oxygen. The ratio of the atoms gives the empirical formula.
cards.11.svg#17: O in the products isn't counted: some of it comes from O₂.
cards.11.key: Burning 2.9 g of a sample gave 8.8 g of CO₂ and 4.5 g of H₂O. These products contain 2.4 g of C and 0.5 g of H, so the sample has no O. The C:H ratio is 2:5, and if M = 58, the formula is C₄H₁₀.
cards.11.once.soru: A substance burns and gives only CO₂ and H₂O. Which elements are certainly in the substance?
cards.11.once.secenekler.0.neden: The O in the products can also come from O₂ in the air. Only C and H are certain.
cards.11.once.secenekler.1.neden: Whether O is present is found by a mass calculation, not by looking at the products.
cards.11.once.secenekler.2.neden: Since H₂O forms, H is present too.
cards.12.p: Compounds that contain only C and H are hydrocarbons. If the molecule has a functional group such as –OH or –COOH, that group largely decides its reactions.
cards.12.key: You will see alkanes, alkenes, alkynes and aromatics in the next topic. The functional group is the part that gives a molecule its character.
cards.12.once.secenekler.0.neden: It contains an O atom. Hydrocarbons contain only C and H.
cards.12.once.secenekler.2.neden: Being a hydrocarbon depends on the elements, not the state.
cards.13.p: Compounds with the same molecular formula but different structures are called isomers. There are chain, position and functional group (for example, −OH) isomers. Ethanol and dimethyl ether are functional group isomers of each other.
cards.13.key: To be isomers, the molecular formulas must first be the same. Pentane and 2-methylbutane are chain isomers.
cards.14.p: A C=C bond cannot rotate because of the π bond. If both carbons of the double bond carry different groups, the isomer is cis when similar groups are on the same side and trans when they are on opposite sides.
cards.14.svg#14: Cl atoms on the same side
cards.14.key: ClHC=CHCl is an example. CH₂=CHCl has no cis-trans isomers, because one of its carbons carries two H atoms.
cards.15.p:
• Organic chemistry studies carbon compounds. CO, CO₂ and carbonates are left out.
• Wöhler's synthesis of urea shook the idea of vital force.
• The angle is 109.5° for sp³, 120° for sp² and 180° for sp. A lone pair narrows the angle.
• A single bond is 1σ, a double bond 1σ+1π and a triple bond 1σ+2π.
• Isomers have the same molecular formula but different structures.
quiz.0.q: Match the carbon atom in each molecule with its hybridization and bond angle.
quiz.0.e: In CO₂, C forms two double bonds, so it is sp hybridized and the angle is 180°. In HCHO, C has one double bond and is sp² hybridized (120°). In CH₃OH, C forms only single bonds and is sp³ hybridized (109.5°).
quiz.1.q: Sort each substance as organic or inorganic.
quiz.1.e: Organic chemistry studies carbon compounds, and the urea Wöhler synthesized is organic too. CO₂, carbonates (CaCO₃), cyanides (KCN) and carbides (CaC₂) contain carbon but count as inorganic.
quiz.2.q: How many sigma (σ) bonds are in the molecule CH₂=CH–C≡CH?
quiz.2.e: Each of the four C–H bonds and three C–C bonds contains one σ bond, so there are 4 + 3 = 7σ in total. The double bond adds another 1π, and the triple bond adds 2π.
quiz.3.q: Burning 4.6 g of a compound containing C, H and O completely gives 8.8 g of CO₂ and 5.4 g of H₂O. What is the empirical formula of the compound? (C = 12, H = 1, O = 16 g/mol)
quiz.3.e: 8.8 g of CO₂ contains 0.2 mol of C (2.4 g). 5.4 g of H₂O is 0.3 mol and contains 0.6 mol of H (0.6 g). Oxygen is 4.6 − 3.0 = 1.6 g, or 0.1 mol. The ratio is 2 : 6 : 1, so the empirical formula is C₂H₆O. If you forget the two H atoms in H₂O, you get C₂H₃O.
quiz.3.y.0: 2.4 g of C and 0.6 g of H add up to 3.0 g. You left out the remaining 1.6 g of oxygen.
quiz.3.y.1: You didn't count the two H atoms in H₂O. 0.3 mol of water gives 0.6 mol of H, so the C:H ratio is 2:6.
quiz.3.y.3: You get 0.2 mol of C, 0.6 mol of H and 0.1 mol of O. The smallest ratio is 2:6:1, which doesn't fit CH₂O.
A:baslik: Carbon and an introduction to organic chemistry
A:ozet: Give carbon four bonds, watch the angle change with the bond type, count σ and π bonds, explore the types of formulas and tell isomers apart.
A:adimlar.0.metin: Attach hydrogen to carbon so that no bond is left open.
A:adimlar.0.gorev.ipucu: The dashed lines are open bonds.
A:adimlar.0.gorev.tamam: This compound is CH₄, methane, the simplest organic compound. The four bonds point to the corners of a regular tetrahedron.
A:adimlar.1.metin: Now two carbons are joined by a double bond. C=C counts as two bonds for each carbon. How many H should attach to each carbon?
A:adimlar.1.gorev.ipucu: A double bond counts as 2 bonds. Bring the bond count up to 4.
A:adimlar.1.gorev.tamam: This compound is C₂H₄, ethene. The double bond makes 2 bonds, and the two H atoms make 2 more. In ethyne (C₂H₂), with a triple bond, each carbon keeps only one H.
A:adimlar.2.metin: The bond type decides the geometry around carbon. Change the bond type and watch the hybrid and the bond angle.
A:adimlar.2.gorev.soru: In CO₂, carbon forms two double bonds (O=C=O). What is carbon's hybrid and the shape of the molecule?
A:adimlar.2.gorev.secenekler.0.neden: sp³ is a carbon with four single bonds. In CO₂, carbon has only two neighbors and no single bonds.
A:adimlar.2.gorev.secenekler.1.neden: An sp² carbon has three neighbors, through one double and two single bonds. In CO₂, carbon has only two O neighbors.
A:adimlar.2.gorev.secenekler.2.neden: A carbon with a triple bond or two double bonds is sp hybridized. O=C=O is linear, with a 180° angle. So the two C=O dipoles cancel, and CO₂ is nonpolar.
A:adimlar.3.metin: A single bond is 1σ, and a triple bond is 1σ + 2π. Count the σ and π bonds in propyne (CH₃–C≡CH).
A:adimlar.3.gorev.ipucu: Count the C–H bonds too. Each one is a σ bond.
A:adimlar.3.gorev.tamam: 4 C–H and 2 C–C bonds make 6σ in total. The triple bond adds another 2π.
A:adimlar.4.metin: The same molecule can be written in different ways. Explore the formulas of butane. You can also tap the tabs at the top.
A:adimlar.4.gorev.soru: Which two molecules have the same empirical formula?
A:adimlar.4.gorev.secenekler.0.neden: The empirical formula of CH₄ is CH₄, and that of C₂H₆ is CH₃. Their C:H ratios differ.
A:adimlar.4.gorev.secenekler.1.neden: Both have a C:H ratio of 1:1, and the empirical formula is CH. To tell them apart, you need the molar mass. Their molar masses are 26 and 78 g/mol.
A:adimlar.4.gorev.secenekler.2.neden: The empirical formula of C₂H₄ is CH₂, and that of C₂H₆ is CH₃. The number of carbons is the same, but the ratio differs.
A:adimlar.5.metin: Four carbons can be arranged in two different ways. Branch the chain and see what changes.
A:adimlar.5.gorev.soru: Which is true for butane and 2-methylpropane?
A:adimlar.5.gorev.secenekler.0.neden: Both have 4 C and 10 H. So the molecular formula is the same (C₄H₁₀).
A:adimlar.5.gorev.secenekler.1.neden: Their boiling points differ (−0.5 °C and −11.7 °C), so they are different substances. One is a straight chain and the other is branched.
A:adimlar.5.gorev.secenekler.2.neden: The molecular formula is the same (C₄H₁₀), but the carbon skeleton differs. This is called chain isomerism. When the structure changes, the properties change too.
A:adimlar.6.metin: In the trans isomer, the two Cl atoms are on opposite sides of the double bond. Put a Cl on the right carbon and flip that carbon to build trans-1,2-dichloroethene.
A:adimlar.6.gorev.ipucu: In the trans isomer, the two Cl atoms are on opposite sides.
A:adimlar.6.gorev.tamam: You built trans-1,2-dichloroethene. The two Cl atoms are on opposite sides, the dipoles cancel, and the molecule is nonpolar. That is why the cis isomer has a higher boiling point.
A:kapanis.0: In stable organic compounds, carbon forms four bonds. C=C counts as two bonds and C≡C as three.
A:kapanis.1: A carbon with only single bonds is sp³ (109.5°), one with a double bond is sp² (120°), and one with a triple bond or two double bonds is sp (180°) hybridized.
A:kapanis.2: A single bond is 1σ, a double bond is 1σ + 1π, and a triple bond is 1σ + 2π. C–H bonds are σ bonds too.
A:kapanis.3: The molecular formula shows the numbers of atoms, and the empirical formula shows the smallest ratio. For example, C₂H₂ and C₆H₆ have the same empirical formula (CH).
A:kapanis.4: Substances with the same molecular formula but different structures are called isomers. Butane and 2-methylpropane are chain isomers. Cis- and trans-dichloroethene are geometric isomers.
